purpose: Real input set for a rebuild of FEMA QUICK-2 (1995), irregular cross-section, Normal Depth mode. Ground section, 1% AEP discharge and slope at one spot on a small Zone A stream near Huntington, WV. Bank stations, Manning's n and slope remain engineer inputs; values here are sourced estimates or suggestions.

units.station: feet (international foot, metres x 3.28084, the factor the TPE page uses)
units.elevation: feet NAVD88, returned directly by USGS EPQS with units=Feet (no conversion by me)

stream.name: Grapevine Branch
stream.receiving_stream: Fourpole Creek (NHD 58000985 / 58000965), about 2,600 ft downstream along the channel; Fourpole flows to the Ohio River
stream.county_state: Cabell County, West Virginia (FIRM panel set DFIRM_ID 54011C, Cabell County)
stream.setting: About 4 miles south-east of downtown Huntington, in the valley followed by 16th Street Road (CR 43)

center_point.note: on the section line; the NHD point at 1,200 m along the reach moved 40 ft toward the right bank so the right end clears the road fill on the right overbank

location.section_orientation: perpendicular to the NHD flowline (bearing taken between points 40 m up and down the line); station 0 is the left end looking downstream

cross_section.method: Same as the TPE page (bzjoe.github.io/TPE): 2-point line, 40 points at equal spacing via turf.along logic (haversine, R = 6,371,008.8 m), each elevation from https://epqs.nationalmap.gov/v1/json?x=<lon>&y=<lat>&units=Feet&output=json. Values rounded to 2 decimals as TPE displays them.
cross_section.dem_source: USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar DEM, project WV_FEMAR3_Southcentral_2018_D19 (EPQS rasterId [58058] for all 40 points, acquisition date 2/5/2020 per EPQS includeDate)

discharge.drainage_area_source: Shape_Area of the StreamStats ss-delineate watershed polygon / 2,589,988.11 m2 per mi2, rounded to 0.01 mi2 (ss-hydro basin-characteristics returned HTTP 502); cross-checked with an equal-area computation of the returned polygon
discharge.citation: Messinger, T., Duda, J.M., Wagner, D.M., O'Shea, P.S., Scott, J.D., and Kandel, C., 2026, Estimation of magnitude and frequency of floods for rural, unregulated streams in and near Virginia and West Virginia: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2025-5110, 85 p., https://doi.org/10.3133/sir20255110 (data through water year 2021). Citation as returned by https://streamstats.usgs.gov/nssservices/citations?regressionregions=GC2081
discharge.method: USGS StreamStats services, following USGS's own workflow notebook (StreamStatsFlowStatisticsWorkflow.ipynb): ss-delineate (GET), nssservices regressionregions/bylocation (POST), scenarios (GET, statisticgroups=2 peak flow), ss-hydro basin characteristics (POST, failed HTTP 502), nssservices scenarios/estimate (POST).

slope.label: ESTIMATE from 3DEP, not a surveyed slope

method_B_least_squares.how: Every 25 m along the NHD flowline from 1,000 ft upstream to 1,000 ft downstream of the section (25 points), local thalweg = lowest 3DEP value (bilinear, 3DEPElevation ImageServer getSamples) across a +/-60 ft window perpendicular to the line; least-squares line through elevation vs distance along the flowline.

method_A_point_pairs.how: (z_upstream - z_downstream) / flowline distance between points 500 ft and 1,000 ft up and down the NHD flowline

slope.streamstats_channel_slope: Not available: ss-hydro basin-characteristics service returned HTTP 502 on every attempt, so CSL1085LFP could not be requested.

bank_stations_suggested.label: SUGGESTION from the 40-point profile, not a field determination
bank_stations_suggested.reasoning: The channel shows as a notch with its low point at station index 16 (205.13 ft, 589.22 ft). Index 14 (179.49 ft) and index 18 (230.77 ft) are the tops of the notch at about the same elevation (591.78 and 591.95 ft): to the right the ground flattens into the floodplain (about 592 to 593.6 ft), to the left it steepens into the valley wall. A tighter alternative is indices 15 and 17 (192.31 and 217.95 ft), the side-slope points nearest the low point.

sources_used.name: Esri Living Atlas 'USA Flood Hazard Reduced Set' (copy of FEMA NFHL S_FLD_HAZ_AR)
WV Flood Tool (WVGISTC) 'FEMA Effective Floodplain' layer
Zone extent along the section (Esri copy, polygon intersect)

nearest_downstream_effective_BFEs.note: FEMA effective BFE lines (Cabell FIRM 54011C) on lower Grapevine Branch where it is Zone AE in Fourpole Creek's backwater; the 590 ft lines are the upstream limit of detailed study below this Zone A section. A computed normal-depth WSE here should come out above 590.

wv_statewide_hecras_1pct.note: WV Flood Tool statewide HEC-RAS 1% depth grid (not FEMA effective, model discharge unknown); WSE = EPQS ground + grid depth at each wet station.

reference_checks_not_inputs.wv_advisory_flood_height: WSEL_01PCT_AFH_Composite returned no data along this section.

streamstats.estimate: https://streamstats.usgs.gov/nssservices/scenarios/estimate?regions=WV  (POST, body = the scenarios response with DRNAREA filled in)

site_selection_notes: Candidates: named NHD flowlines (MapServer/6) inside Zone A polygons of the Cabell (54011C) and Wayne (54099C) FIRMs, then screened for ground elevation, the WV statewide HEC-RAS 1% depth grid and distance to roads (USGS National Map transportation layers).

First choice, Davis Creek (NHD 76169965, 38.3898, -82.3290, 5.2 mi2, Zone A) was REJECTED: its whole lower reach sits in the Guyandotte River's 1% backwater. The WV HEC-RAS grid gives a flat WSE of about 555 ft over 2.5 km while the bed there is about 537 ft, so normal depth would understate the flood by many feet.

Grapevine Branch was chosen: Zone A, bed about 589 ft at the section; the nearest effective BFE downstream (590 ft, Fourpole Creek backwater, about 1,300 ft away) is below the WV HEC-RAS 1% WSE here (about 595 ft), which slopes with the bed, so normal depth should govern at the section; the section is about 1,600 ft from the 16th St Rd crossing upstream and 1,500 ft from the Mount Union Rd crossing downstream, and about 190 ft from James Kilowatt Ln.
caveats: Lidar bare-earth DEMs do not see below water: the channel bottom here is the water surface at acquisition (WV FEMA R3 lidar, 2018 to 2020), so channel area below it is missing. At this stream size the channel shows only as a 2 to 3 ft notch caught by 2 to 3 stations.
40 stations over 500 ft gives 12.8 ft spacing; the main channel is roughly 20 to 30 ft wide, so bank positions are coarse.

The right overbank holds a raised strip (about 598 ft) and then a flat bench near 595 to 596 ft that is probably a lane or yard, then higher ground near 602 ft that is likely road fill. Treat the area behind the raised strip as possibly ineffective flow if the computed WSE is below about 598 ft.
The discharge is a regional regression estimate (ASEp about 40%, 90% prediction interval 624 to 2,310 cfs), for rural unregulated streams; the basin includes suburban development along 16th St Rd.

DRNAREA was taken from the StreamStats delineation polygon because ss-hydro returned HTTP 502; StreamStats' own DRNAREA for this basin may differ in the last digit. The 1% flow is the same (1,200 cfs) for 2.6984 or 2.70 mi2 at the service's 3-significant-figure rounding.
Slope is a DEM estimate along the NHD line; pools and riffles make the local value vary (0.0029 to 0.0037 ft/ft across methods).
The FEMA zone comes from two copies of the effective NFHL (Esri Living Atlas and WV Flood Tool), not from hazards.fema.gov, which was unreachable from this machine.
The NHD high-resolution line is offset from the lidar channel by a few tens of feet in places; the section crosses the lidar low point, which is what matters for the hydraulics.
Every elevation here was fetched directly from the USGS service; none is synthetic.
